thread:
Maria: bumping this here — enterprise customer (proj: proj-acme) says embeddings suddenly started returning vectors of length 1536 -> 128. Their downstream cosine similarity exploded and search ranking broke. They also reported a spike in token/embedding billing.

Maria: repro steps they sent: POST /v1/embeddings with model "embed-large-v1" in JSON body, content-type application/json. Example curl they gave:

Maria: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer org_sk_live_ABCDEF" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":"some text"}'
```

Maria: response vector length they got: 128

Jake: quick thought — looks like they're using an org-scoped key in Authorization. If the request is authenticated at org-level we sometimes route to an org-default project/model mapping (legacy fallback) which can pick a smaller embedding model. Can you paste response headers?

Maria: headers from their raw response (they redacted some):

Maria: ```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Model: embed-small-v1
X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 124
X-Request-Id: req_01G...
```

Maria: so server actually returned X-Redwood-Model: embed-small-v1 even though they set model embed-large-v1 in payload.

Sophia: yep that's the smoking gun. Our routing logic: if the auth key is an org API key (org_sk_...), we require a project header (x-redwood-project or x-rw-project-id) to select a project-scoped model. If missing, code falls back to an org-default embedding model which for some customers is the smaller 128-dim model. That explains dimension mismatch and cost/throughput changes.

Jake: two likely causes: 1) customer sent an org-level key and no project header, or 2) sent the wrong header name (e.g., X-Project instead of X-Redwood-Project). Also some SDK versions silently pass org keys in client config.

Maria: customer confirms they were moving from an app with per-project keys to a centralized org key after consolidation. They didn't set the project header in new code.

Will_BillingBot: FYI — when model downgraded to embed-small-v1 we see lower per-call token cost but they complained about a billing spike — could be due to retries (client layer re-requesting with different model) or increased ingestion because similarity failed. We'll keep a note but not billing-urgent yet.

Sophia: repro steps for support to confirm locally:

Sophia: 1) Use an org key in Authorization and omit x-redwood-project-id header -> server should return embed-small-v1 (128 dims).

Sophia: 2) Use same org key but include header `X-Redwood-Project: proj-acme` -> server should honor request body and return embed-large-v1 (1536 dims).

Sophia: Example curls:

Sophia: ```bash
# wrong (org-level, no project header) -> fallback small model
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer org_sk_live_ABCDEF" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":"hello world"}' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'

# correct (include project header) -> project mapping used
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer org_sk_live_ABCDEF" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Project: proj-acme" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":"hello world"}' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
```

Maria: if they use a project-scoped API key instead (sk_proj_live_...) that also works without X-Redwood-Project header.

Jake: additional debug hints to give customer: check response header `X-Redwood-Model` or `x-rw-selected-model` — that'll show what model actually served. Also our telemetry includes a `selected_model` field in request logs. If they paste a `X-Request-Id` we can look it up.

Maria: asked customer to send `X-Request-Id` from one of the failing calls — they sent `req_01Gxyz` (we have logs).

Jake: pulled trace for req_01Gxyz: `auth_type=org_key, project_header=missing, requested_model=embed-large-v1, selected_model=embed-small-v1, reason=fallback-org-default`. Forwarding to runtime team just in case.

Sophia: longer-term fix: SDKs should warn if org key used without project header when model param is an embeddings model (warn about dimension mismatch). We'll add a validation. For now, recommended mitigation steps for customer:

Sophia: - Preferred: use project-scoped key (sk_proj_...)
Sophia: - Alternatively add `X-Redwood-Project: proj-acme` header on requests when using org-scoped key
Sophia: - If they need to keep org key and force a model regardless of project defaults, they can set `model` param to an exact spec and we will honor it only if project entitlements allow it; but better to use the header or proj key.

Maria: customer accepted adding header; they pushed fix and verified vectors are length 1536 again. Their ranking recovered.

Jake: follow-up actions for us:

Jake: - (ENG) add a clear 4xx warning when org key used and model param mismatches org default (low risk change)
Jake: - (DEVEX) add note in SDK docs about org vs project keys and required headers for embeddings
Jake: - (SUPPORT) update KB article with repro + curls + example response headers

Sophia: I filed runtime ticket RW-3582 to ensure X-Redwood-Model header is always set in responses (if not already) and to add one-line explanation in the header when fallback happened.

Maria: noting cost spike: ask billing to monitor for any charges that were caused by repeated retries or extra ingestion.

Will_BillingBot: watching invoices for proj-acme and will flag anomalies.

ingest-bot: automated note: logs attached to ticket #T-1223, trace req_01Gxyz, storage path s3://redwood-support/proj-acme/2024-04-xx/req_01Gxyz.json

Maria: closing loop with customer now, they were able to confirm fix. Will file KB and mark resolved after docs updated. :thumbsup:

Jake: thanks — leaving runtime ticket open until header/validation changes are in prod.

Sophia: cool, thanks team.
